mainTopic: Personal prayers of the אמוראים after the עמידה (including the source of אלהי נצור), favorite sayings of the חכמים, women's reward for supporting Torah, and farewell blessings of the study hall.
overview: This עמוד opens by finishing a list, begun on the previous עמוד, of private prayers that great אמוראים said after the עמידה. It completes רב ספרא's prayer for peace, then brings the prayers of רבי אלכסנדרי, רבא, and מר בריה דרבינא. מר בריה דרבינא's prayer is the source of our אלהי נצור. Next comes רב ששת's prayer on a fast day, asking that the fat and blood he lost count as a קרבן. The גמרא then moves to sayings the חכמים often repeated: רבי יוחנן on finishing ספר איוב, and the favorite sayings of רבי מאיר, the רבנן of יבנה, אביי, רבא, and רב. These teach about a good name, sincere intent, spreading peace, learning לשמה, and the reward of עולם הבא. The גמרא then teaches that women receive a great promise because they make Torah learning possible for their children and husbands. It ends with the farewell blessings the רבנן gave when leaving the study hall, and two explanations of the פסוק "אלופינו מסבלים."

steps.title: End of רב ספרא's prayer for peace
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא's prayer ends by asking for peace among the angels, among the sages, and among Torah students. It also asks that those who learn for the wrong reasons come to learn for the right reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: …in the heavenly group, and in the earthly group, and among the students who study Your Torah, whether they study it for its own sake or not for its own sake. And may it be Your will that all those who study not for its own sake will come to study for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The text picks up in the middle of רב ספרא's prayer from the previous עמוד, which asks God to place peace in different groups. Here we read the end of that prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer moves from the heavenly 'entourage' (the angels) to the earthly 'entourage' (the חכמים) and then to the students. It does not reject people who learn שלא לשמה. Instead it prays that they will grow into learning לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Entourage or group. 'Above' means the angels; 'below' means the sages.
For its own sake, meaning learning Torah purely to serve God.
Not for its own sake, meaning learning for honor or other personal motives.
May it be (Your) will, the standard opening of a request.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new prayer. It is the second half of רב ספרא's prayer, which began on the previous עמוד ('may it be Your will to place peace…').

phrases.english: in the heavenly entourage (the angels);
phrases.notes: Continues 'that You place peace…' from the previous page.

phrases.english: and in the earthly entourage (the sages);
and among the students who study Your Torah,
whether they study it for its own sake
or study it not for its own sake.
And all those who study not for its own sake,
may it be Your will that they come to study for its own sake.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּפָמַלְיָא שֶׁל מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב ספרא's prayer, which started on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ספרא prayed for peace among the angels, the sages, and the students, and that those who learn שלא לשמה come to learn לשמה.

steps.title: רבי אלכסנדרי's prayer for light
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלכסנדרי asked God to place us in a place of light and not of darkness, and to keep our hearts from fainting and our eyes from growing dim.
steps.simpleTranslation: After his prayer, רבי אלכסנדרי said this: 'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You place us in a corner of light and not in a corner of darkness, and do not let our heart become sick, and do not let our eyes grow dark.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next אמורא on the list and quotes his personal prayer after the עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Light' and 'darkness' are images for a life of good fortune versus trouble (many explain light as Torah and darkness as its absence). The request about the heart and eyes asks to be protected from the pain and despair that trouble brings.

keyTerms.meaning: After his prayer, meaning after finishing the עמידה.
A corner of light, an image for a good, bright place in life.
A corner of darkness, an image for trouble and gloom.
Become sick or faint, from the root meaning pain or illness.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אָלֶכְּסַנְדְרִי בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Alexandri, after his prayer, said this:
'May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that You place us in a corner of light,
and do not place us in a corner of darkness;
and let our heart not become faint,
and let our eyes not grow dim.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אָלֶכְּסַנְדְרִי בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next entry in the list of post-עמידה prayers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלכסנדרי asked to be placed in light and not in darkness, and to be kept from faintness of heart and dimness of eyes.

steps.title: Another version of who said that prayer
steps.stepSummary: Some say that the 'light and darkness' prayer actually belonged to רב המנונא, and not to רבי אלכסנדרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: this prayer was the one רב המנונא used to pray.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second tradition about who said the prayer just quoted. This sets up the next step, where רבי אלכסנדרי is given a different prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this version, the 'light and darkness' prayer is credited to רב המנונא. רבי אלכסנדרי is then credited with a different prayer, which the next step quotes. The words of the prayers stay the same; only who said them changes.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say. It introduces another version of a tradition.
Would pray it, meaning he used to say this prayer.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
this one, Rav Hamnuna would pray it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי, הָא רַב הַמְנוּנָא מְצַלֵּי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different attribution for the prayer in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to another version, the 'light and darkness' prayer was רב המנונא's.

steps.title: רבי אלכסנדרי's prayer: what holds us back
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, רבי אלכסנדרי tells God that we truly want to do His will. Two things stop us: the יצר הרע and the rule of foreign kingdoms. He asks God to save us from both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלכסנדרי, after he prayed, said this: 'Master of the worlds, it is clear and known before You that we want to do Your will. And who stops us? The yeast in the dough and the rule of the nations. May it be Your will to save us from their hands, so that we return to doing the laws of Your will with a complete heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the second version, the גמרא quotes the prayer that רבי אלכסנדרי said after his תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer says that a Jew's real inner will is to serve God. Sin comes from obstacles, not from his true self. 'Yeast in the dough' is the יצר הרע, which puffs a person up from inside. 'Rule of the kingdoms' is the outside pressure of the nations. The request is to remove both obstacles so that we can serve God completely.

keyTerms.meaning: It is revealed and known before You.
The yeast in the dough, a name for the יצר הרע.
Being ruled by the (foreign) kingdoms.
Holds back or prevents.
A complete, whole heart.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous source for the idea that a Jew's true will is to do God's will, and that sin comes from outside forces such as the יצר הרע and גלות.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אָלֶכְּסַנְדְרִי בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Alexandri, after he prayed, said this:
'Master of the worlds, it is revealed and known before You
that our will is to do Your will;
and who holds us back?
The yeast in the dough (the evil inclination) and the rule of the kingdoms.
May it be Your will that You save us from their hands,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָשׁוּב לַעֲשׂוֹת חוּקֵּי רְצוֹנְךָ בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם״.
phrases.english: and we will return to doing the laws of Your will with a whole heart.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אָלֶכְּסַנְדְרִי בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the alternative version by giving רבי אלכסנדרי's own prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We want to do God's will, but the יצר הרע and foreign rule stop us, so we ask to be saved from both.

steps.title: רבא's humble prayer of confession
steps.stepSummary: רבא describes how small and unworthy he is before God. He asks never to sin again, and asks that his past sins be cleansed through mercy and not through suffering.
steps.simpleTranslation: After his prayer, רבא said this: 'My God, before I was formed I was not worthy, and now that I have been formed it is as if I was not formed. I am dust in my life, all the more so in my death. I am before You like a vessel full of shame and embarrassment. May it be Your will, ה׳ my God, that I not sin again. And what I have sinned before You, wipe away in Your great mercy, but not through suffering and bad illnesses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next אמורא, רבא, and his personal prayer after the עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer has two parts. First, רבא humbles himself: he says he has no worth before or after his creation, and uses a קל וחומר (if dust in life, surely in death). Then he makes his requests: to stop sinning, and to be cleansed of past sins in a gentle way, through mercy, and not through יסורין.

keyTerms.meaning: Worthy or significant.
All the more so, an argument from a lesser case to a greater one.
Shame and humiliation.
Scour or cleanse (said here of sins).
Suffering or afflictions.

steps.whyThisMatters: This prayer is part of the וידוי we say on יום כיפור (at the end of the עמידה), as the next step points out.

phrases.english: Rava, after his prayer, said this:
'My God, before I was formed I was not worthy,
and now that I have been formed, it is as if I had not been formed.
I am dust in my life,
all the more so in my death.

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אֲנִי לְפָנֶיךָ כִּכְלִי מָלֵא בּוּשָׁה וּכְלִימָּה.
phrases.english: I am before You like a vessel full of shame and humiliation.
May it be Your will, Lord my God,
that I will not sin again,
and what I have sinned before You,
cleanse in Your great mercy,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין וָחֳלָאִים רָעִים״.
phrases.english: but not through suffering and bad illnesses.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא בָּתַר צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side note about attribution, the גמרא returns to the main list of prayers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא humbled himself before God and asked to stop sinning and to be cleansed of past sins through mercy, not suffering.

steps.title: The same words are רב המנונא זוטי's יום כיפור confession
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבא's prayer is the same as the וידוי that רב המנונא זוטי said on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the confession of רב המנונא זוטי on יום כיפור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short side note: the text of רבא's prayer is identical to another sage's יום כיפור confession.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the prayer itself. The note tells us that this text also served as a formal וידוי, which explains why it later entered the יום כיפור liturgy.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as.
Confession of sins.
יום כיפור (Aramaic).

phrases.english: And this is the confession of Rav Hamnuna Zuti
on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ וִידּוּי דְרַב הַמְנוּנָא זוּטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies רבא's prayer with a known יום כיפור confession.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's prayer is identical to רב המנונא זוטי's יום כיפור וידוי.

steps.title: מר בריה דרבינא's prayer: the source of אלהי נצור
steps.stepSummary: When מר בריה דרבינא finished his תפלה, he asked God to guard his speech and give him humility. He asked for an open heart to Torah and the drive to pursue מצוות. He asked to be protected from harm and from those who plot against him, and he closed with יהיו לרצון.
steps.simpleTranslation: When מר the son of רבינא would finish his prayer, he said this: 'My God, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceit. To those who curse me let my soul be silent, and let my soul be like dust to everyone. Open my heart to Your Torah, and let my soul run after Your מצוות. Save me from bad happenings, from the יצר הרע, from a bad woman, and from all bad things that rush to come into the world. And all who plan evil against me, quickly ruin their plan and spoil their thoughts. May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be pleasing before You, ה׳, my Rock and my Redeemer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next prayer on the list, from מר בריה דרבינא. This is the prayer we say today at the end of every עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prayer moves in order. It starts with control of speech and humility (not answering those who curse). It then asks for spiritual growth in Torah and מצוות, then for protection from outside dangers and enemies. It closes with the פסוק from תהלים (19:15), 'יהיו לרצון'.

keyTerms.meaning: Guard or protect.
Deceit or trickery.
Will be silent (not answering back).
A bad occurrence or mishap.
That suddenly rush or break out.
The thoughts or meditation of my heart.

steps.whatToRemember: These prayers show that the אמוראים added personal requests after the עמידה. מר בריה דרבינא's prayer became the standard אלהי נצור that all of us say at the end of שמונה עשרה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the direct source of אלהי נצור in our סידור, and of the custom to end the עמידה with 'יהיו לרצון'.

phrases.aramaic: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי:
phrases.english: Mar, son of Ravina, when he would finish his prayer, said this:
'My God, guard my tongue from evil
and my lips from speaking deceit.
To those who curse me, let my soul be silent,
and let my soul be like dust to all.
Open my heart to Your Torah,
and let my soul pursue Your מצוות.
And save me from a bad mishap, from the evil inclination,
and from a bad woman,
and from all evils that suddenly rush to come into the world.
And all who plan evil against me,
quickly undo their counsel and spoil their plans.

phrases.aramaic: יִהְיוּ לְרָצוֹן אִמְרֵי פִי וְהֶגְיוֹן לִבִּי
phrases.english: May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be pleasing
before You, Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים צְלוֹתֵיהּ אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next entry in the list of post-עמידה prayers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מר בריה דרבינא ended his תפלה with אלהי נצור, asking for guarded speech, humility, devotion to Torah, protection, and acceptance of his prayer.

steps.title: רב ששת's prayer after a fast
steps.stepSummary: After praying on a fast day, רב ששת asked God to count the fat and blood he lost through fasting as if he had offered them as a קרבן on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב ששת sat in a fast, after he prayed he said: 'Master of the world, You know that when the בית המקדש stood, a person who sinned brought a קרבן. Only its fat and blood were offered, and he was forgiven. Now I have fasted, and my own fat and blood have become less. May it be Your will that my lost fat and blood count as if I offered them before You on the מזבח, and may You accept me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more personal prayer, this time one that רב ששת said after his תפלה on a fast day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת compares himself to a קרבן. In the מקדש, the fat (חלב) and blood (דם) of the animal went on the מזבח and brought atonement. Fasting shrinks a person's own fat and blood, so he asks that this loss bring him the same atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: A fast day
A sacrifice offered in the בית המקדש
Fat and blood, the parts of a sacrifice placed on the altar
The altar
And may You accept me / find me pleasing

steps.whyThisMatters: This prayer shows the idea that in exile a personal fast can stand in for a קרבן. Many people still say this prayer at מנחה on a fast day.

phrases.aramaic: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת כִּי הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא,
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, when he would sit in a fast,
after he prayed, he said this:
'Master of the worlds, it is revealed before You
that when the Temple is standing,
a person sins and brings a sacrifice.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מַקְרִיבִין מִמֶּנּוּ, אֶלָּא חֶלְבּוֹ וְדָמוֹ,
phrases.english: And they offer from it only its fat and its blood,
and he is forgiven.
And now I have sat in a fast
and my fat and my blood have become less.
May it be Your will
that my fat and my blood that became less

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרַבְתִּיו לְפָנֶיךָ עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ,
phrases.english: be as if I offered it before You on the altar,
phrases.notes: The fasting stands in for the sacrifice

phrases.english: and may You accept me.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת כִּי הֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא, בָּתַר דִּמְצַלֵּי אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of personal prayers said after תפלה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fasting reduces one's fat and blood, and one may pray that this count as a קרבן for atonement.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's words on finishing ספר איוב
steps.stepSummary: After finishing ספר איוב, רבי יוחנן said that everyone dies. What matters is living with Torah and a good name, and he quoted שלמה המלך: a good name is better than fine oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן finished ספר איוב, he said: 'A person will end up dying, and an animal will end up being slaughtered. Everyone is headed toward death. Happy is the one who grew up in Torah, worked hard in Torah, gave pleasure to his Creator, grew up with a good name, and left the world with a good name. About him שלמה said: A good name is better than good oil, and the day of death is better than the day of birth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from prayers said after תפלה to sayings the חכמים said at other times. Here it brings what רבי יוחנן said when he finished learning ספר איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since death comes to everyone, death is not the real tragedy. What counts is how a person lived. Someone who lived with Torah and kept a good name to the end is better off on his day of death than on his day of birth.

keyTerms.meaning: Finishing or completing (a book of study)
The book of Job
Pleasure / satisfaction to his Creator
A good name / reputation
Departs (this world)

steps.confusionAlert: 'The day of death is better than the day of birth' does not praise death itself. It means a person who lived well arrives at death having gained more than he had at birth.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים סִפְרָא דְאִיּוֹב, אָמַר הָכִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan, when he would finish the book of Job, said this:
'The end of a person is to die,
and the end of an animal is to be slaughtered,
and all are headed toward death.
Happy is one who grew up in Torah
and whose labor is in Torah,
and who gives pleasure to his Creator,
and who grew up with a good name
and left the world with a good name.
And about him Solomon said:
'A good name is better than good oil,
and the day of death than the day of his birth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּי הֲוָה מְסַיֵּים סִפְרָא דְאִיּוֹב, אָמַר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from prayers after תפלה to sayings of the חכמים on other occasions
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since everyone dies, true happiness belongs to one who lived in Torah and left the world with a good name.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's favorite saying
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר often repeated a message spoken in God's voice: learn My ways with your whole heart, keep Torah and fear of Me close, guard your speech, stay pure, and I will be with you everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: A saying that was always in רבי מאיר's mouth: 'Learn with all your heart and all your soul to know My ways, and to be diligent at the doors of My Torah. Guard My Torah in your heart, and keep fear of Me before your eyes. Guard your mouth from every sin, and purify and sanctify yourself from every guilt and sin. And I will be with you in every place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a saying that רבי מאיר used to repeat often. It is spoken as if God is talking to the person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying lists what a person must do: learn deeply, hold on to Torah, keep יראת שמים in view, guard his speech, and keep himself pure. Then it gives the promise: if you do these things, God will be with you wherever you go.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'pearl in his mouth', meaning a saying someone often repeated
Study / learn thoroughly
To be diligent / persistent
Fear of Me (יראת שמים)
Guilt and sin

phrases.english: A saying often in the mouth of Rabbi Meir:
'Learn with all your heart and with all your soul
to know My ways,
and to be diligent at the doors of My Torah.
Guard My Torah in your heart,
and before your eyes let fear of Me be.
Guard your mouth from all sin,

phrases.aramaic: וְטַהֵר וְקַדֵּשׁ עַצְמְךָ מִכָּל אַשְׁמָה וְעָוֹן.
phrases.english: and purify and sanctify yourself from all guilt and iniquity.
And I will be with you in every place.'
phrases.notes: The promise that follows from doing all the above

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another favorite saying of a חכם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Devoted Torah learning, יראת שמים, guarded speech, and purity bring God's presence with a person everywhere.

steps.title: The רבנן of יבנה on respecting the working man
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן of יבנה taught that a Torah scholar and a field worker are both God's creatures, each devoted to his own work. Learning more Torah does not make one better, as long as each person directs his heart to Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: A saying often in the mouths of the רבנן of יבנה: 'I am a creature of God, and my friend is a creature of God. My work is in the city, and his work is in the field. I get up early for my work, and he gets up early for his work. Just as he does not try to take over my work, I do not try to take over his work. And in case you say: I do a lot of Torah and he does only a little, we have learned: whether one does a lot or a little, what matters is that he directs his heart to Heaven.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the series of favorite sayings with one from the רבנן of יבנה. It teaches a Torah scholar not to look down on a simple working person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both men are God's creations, and both work hard at their own job. The saying then answers a likely objection, 'but I learn more Torah', with a teaching from קרבנות: a big offering and a small one are equal, as long as the intent is לשם שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: A creature (of God)
Rises early
Presumes to take over / claims for himself
One who does much and one who does little
That he directs his heart toward Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: These sayings share one theme: what God values is sincere intent and a life of devotion. רב ששת's fast counts as a קרבן, a good name outweighs fine oil, and a small effort with a pure heart equals a large one.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Whether one does much or little' does not mean learning less Torah is just as good in general. It means a person may not look down on someone whose role lets him learn less, as long as that person serves God sincerely.

phrases.english: A saying often in the mouths of the Sages of Yavneh:
'I am a creature, and my fellow is a creature.
My work is in the city
and his work is in the field.
I rise early for my work,
and he rises early for his work.
Just as he does not presume to take over my work,
so I do not presume to take over his work.

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר: אֲנִי מַרְבֶּה, וְהוּא מַמְעִיט —
phrases.english: And perhaps you will say: I do much and he does little.
phrases.notes: Raises a possible objection inside the saying

phrases.english: We have learned: one who does much and one who does little are equal,
phrases.notes: Originally said about large and small offerings

phrases.english: as long as he directs his heart to Heaven.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמַּיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן דְּיַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another favorite saying, using the same מרגלא בפומיה formula
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Torah scholar must not look down on a laborer. What matters is not the amount one does but sincere intent לשם שמים.

steps.title: אביי's saying: be clever in יראת שמים and spread peace
steps.stepSummary: אביי often said that a person should use clever ways to serve God, answer softly, and increase peace with everyone, even a stranger, so that he is loved by God and by people.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי used to say: A person should always be clever in fear of Heaven. "A soft answer turns away anger." He should increase peace with his brothers, his relatives, and every person, even a non-Jew in the market, so that he will be loved above, pleasant below, and accepted by people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another favorite saying, this time from אביי, about how to act wisely and peacefully with people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being "clever" here does not mean tricky. It means using smart strategies to keep the peace, like answering gently when someone is angry. The goal has two sides: being loved by God (above) and being liked by people (below).

keyTerms.meaning: A saying that was often in his mouth; his favorite saying
Clever and strategic in fear of Heaven
A soft, gentle answer
Increases peace
Accepted and well-liked by people

phrases.english: A saying that was often in the mouth of Abaye:
A person should always be clever in fear of Heaven.
"A soft answer turns away anger."

phrases.aramaic: וּמַרְבֶּה שָׁלוֹם עִם אֶחָיו וְעִם קְרוֹבָיו
phrases.english: And he should increase peace with his brothers and with his relatives

phrases.aramaic: וְעִם כָּל אָדָם וַאֲפִילּוּ עִם גּוֹי בַּשּׁוּק,
phrases.english: and with every person, even with a non-Jew in the marketplace,

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא אָהוּב לְמַעְלָה וְנֶחְמָד לְמַטָּה,
phrases.english: so that he will be loved above and pleasant below,
and he will be accepted by people.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of favorite sayings of the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Use clever, gentle strategies to keep the peace with everyone, so you are loved by God and by people.

steps.title: No one ever greeted רבן יוחנן בן זכאי first
steps.stepSummary: A short report about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: he always greeted everyone first, even a stranger in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבן יוחנן בן זכאי that no person ever greeted him first, not even a non-Jew in the market.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a short story that shows אביי's teaching about spreading peace being lived out by a great sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said to spread peace even with a stranger in the market. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי actually did this: he was always the first to say שלום, to anyone at all. The story turns the advice into a real-life example.

keyTerms.meaning: They said about him (introduces a report about a sage)
Greeted him first; said שלום before him
Ever; at any time

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: They said about Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
that no person ever greeted him first,
not even a non-Jew in the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows אביי's advice about peace, even with a stranger in the market, carried out by a great sage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי always greeted everyone first, even a stranger.

steps.title: רבא's saying: the goal of wisdom is תשובה and good deeds, done לשמה
steps.stepSummary: רבא often said that the purpose of Torah wisdom is תשובה and good deeds, not learning that makes a person arrogant toward his parents and teachers. He proves from a פסוק that the benefit goes only to those who learn and act לשמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא used to say: The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds. A person should not read Torah and learn משנה and then kick at his father, his mother, his teacher, or someone greater than him in wisdom or in number. As it says: "The beginning of wisdom is fear of God; good understanding to all who do them." It does not say "to those who do," but "to those who do them": to those who do it for its own sake, not to those who do it not for its own sake. Anyone who does it not for its own sake, it would be better for him not to have been created.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's favorite saying: Torah learning must lead to good behavior, and it must be done for the right reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא first says what learning is for: תשובה and good deeds, not pride that leads a person to disrespect his parents and teachers. He then reads the extra word "them" in "עושיהם" to mean doing the מצוות properly, לשמה. He ends with a strong warning about learning שלא לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The goal or purpose of wisdom
Repentance and good deeds
Kicks at; treats with contempt
For its own sake; for the right reason
It would be better for him not to have been created

steps.confusionAlert: Elsewhere the גמרא says a person should learn even שלא לשמה, because it will lead him to learn לשמה. These do not contradict. תוספות explains that רבא here means someone who learns for a bad purpose, like using Torah to put others down. Learning for a weaker reason, like honor or reward, is still allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step sets the standard that Torah learning is measured by how it changes a person's character and actions, not only by how much he knows.

phrases.english: A saying that was often in the mouth of Rava:
The goal of wisdom is repentance and good deeds,
so that a person should not read Torah and learn Mishnah
and then kick at his father, his mother, and his teacher

phrases.aramaic: וּבְמִי שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל מִמֶּנּוּ בְּחָכְמָה וּבְמִנְיָן,
phrases.english: and at someone greater than him in wisdom or in number,
phrases.notes: "In number" may mean in age, or in the number of students who learn from him.

phrases.english: as it says: "The beginning of wisdom is fear of God,
good understanding to all who do them."
It does not say "to those who do," but "to those who do them":
to those who do it for its own sake,
and not to those who do it not for its own sake.
And anyone who does it not for its own sake,
it would be better for him had he not been created.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next favorite saying in the series, now about the purpose of Torah learning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Torah wisdom must lead to תשובה and good deeds and be done לשמה. Learning שלא לשמה, in the bad sense, is worse than never being created.

steps.title: רב's saying: עולם הבא is not like this world
steps.stepSummary: רב often said that עולם הבא has no eating, drinking, having children, business, jealousy, hatred, or competition. Instead the צדיקים sit with crowns on their heads and enjoy the radiance of the שכינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב used to say: עולם הבא is not like this world. In עולם הבא there is no eating, no drinking, no having children, no business, no jealousy, no hatred, and no competition. Instead, the צדיקים sit with their crowns on their heads and enjoy the radiance of the שכינה, as it says: "And they saw God, and they ate and drank."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's favorite saying, which describes what עולם הבא is like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב first lists everything from this world that will not exist there: physical needs, and the bad feelings that come from them. Then he says what will be there: the צדיקים enjoying closeness to the שכינה. The פסוק shows that seeing God can nourish a person the way food and drink do.

keyTerms.meaning: The World to Come
Business dealings; buying and selling
Competition; rivalry
The radiance of the Divine Presence
And they saw (beheld)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the פסוק "they ate and drank" as meaning there is food in עולם הבא. רב just said there is none. The point is that seeing God satisfied them as if they had eaten and drunk.
steps.whatToRemember: These favorite sayings teach a full picture: be gentle and spread peace (אביי), let Torah lead to good deeds done לשמה (רבא), and know that the final reward is closeness to the שכינה, not physical pleasure (רב).

phrases.english: A saying that was often in the mouth of Rav:
The World to Come is not like this world.
In the World to Come there is
no eating and no drinking,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה וְלֹא מַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן
phrases.english: no having children and no business dealings,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא קִנְאָה וְלֹא שִׂנְאָה וְלֹא תַּחֲרוּת,
phrases.english: no jealousy, no hatred, and no competition,
rather, the righteous sit
with their crowns on their heads
and enjoy the radiance of the Divine Presence,
as it says: "And they saw God,
and they ate and drank."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְגְּלָא בְּפוּמֵּיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of favorite sayings, now describing the reward in עולם הבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עולם הבא has no physical needs or rivalries. The צדיקים enjoy the radiance of the שכינה.

steps.title: God's greater promise to women
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that God promised women a greater reward than men, and brings a פסוק from ישעיה as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The promise God made to women is greater than the one He made to men, as the פסוק says: "Women at ease, rise up, hear My voice; confident daughters, listen to My word."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a new statement: women received a bigger promise from God than men did. It proves this from a פסוק that calls women "at ease" and "confident."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on the words שאננות (at ease) and בוטחות (confident). Being calm and secure is a sign of special reward, and the פסוק gives this description to women only. This statement sets up the next question: what do women do to earn it?

keyTerms.meaning: A promise
At ease, calm and secure
Confident, trusting
As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: Greater is the promise that He promised them
the Holy One, Blessed be He, to women
more than to men,
as it is said:
"Women at ease, rise up, hear My voice;
confident daughters, listen to My word."

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּדוֹלָה הַבְטָחָה שֶׁהִבְטִיחָן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new independent אגדה statement in the collection of teachings on this דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God's promise of reward to women is greater than His promise to men, as shown by ישעיה ל״ב:ט.

steps.title: רב asks how women earn this reward
steps.stepSummary: רב asks רבי חייא what women do to earn their reward.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said to רבי חייא: "By what do women earn their merit?"
steps.whatsHappening: רב asks a question that sets up the next step. If women get such a great promise, what are they doing to deserve it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women are not obligated in תלמוד תורה the way men are, and Torah study is the main source of merit. So רב wants to know where their merit comes from. This is a real question for information, not a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: By what? With what?
They earn merit, they deserve reward

phrases.english: Rav said to Rabbi Chiya:
By what do women earn merit?

steps.triggerLanguage: נָשִׁים בְּמַאי זָכְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the reward described in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What actions earn women their great reward?

steps.title: Women earn merit by supporting Torah learning
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא answers that women earn merit by bringing their children to learn, sending their husbands to learn, and waiting for their husbands to come home.
steps.simpleTranslation: They earn it by bringing their sons to the synagogue to learn to read, by sending their husbands to learn in the study hall, and by waiting for their husbands until they come back from the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers רב's question. Women earn their reward by making the Torah learning of their children and husbands possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three actions are listed: bringing the children to learn (בְּאַקְרוֹיֵי), sending the husbands to learn (בְּאַתְנוֹיֵי), and patiently waiting for the husbands to return (נָטְרִין). The point is that whoever enables Torah learning shares in its reward. The patience of waiting, often late into the night, is counted as a merit on its own.

keyTerms.meaning: By having them read, bringing them to learn to read
The synagogue, where children were taught
By having them learn, sending them to study
The study hall of the Sages
They wait for

steps.whatToRemember: Women's great reward comes from enabling Torah: bringing children to learn, sending husbands to learn, and waiting for them to return.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for the idea that someone who supports and enables Torah learning shares in its reward.

phrases.english: By bringing their sons to read in the synagogue,
and by sending their husbands to learn in the study hall,
and they wait for their husbands
until they come back from the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאַקְרוֹיֵי בְּנַיְיהוּ לְבֵי כְנִישְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רב's question in step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women earn merit by bringing children to learn Torah, sending husbands to study, and waiting for them to return.

steps.title: The farewell blessing at the study hall of רבי אמי
steps.stepSummary: When the רבנן left the study hall of רבי אמי (or רבי חנינא), they blessed one another with a long poetic blessing about this world, עולם הבא, and a life filled with Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the רבנן took leave of the study hall of רבי אמי (some say רבי חנינא), they said to each other: "May you see your world in your lifetime, may your end be life in עולם הבא, and may your hope last for generations. May your heart think understanding, your mouth speak wisdom, and your tongue whisper praises. May your eyelids look straight ahead, your eyes shine with the light of Torah, and your face glow like the brightness of the sky. May your lips pour out knowledge, your kidneys rejoice in what is upright, and your feet run to hear the words of the Ancient of Days."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports the blessing the רבנן gave each other when they finished learning and left the study hall. It is a long, poetic blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing has two parts. The first wishes the learner good in this world, in עולם הבא, and through his descendants. The second goes through the parts of the body (heart, mouth, tongue, eyelids, eyes, face, lips, kidneys, feet) and asks that each one be filled with Torah and holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking leave, departing
And some say (a different version of who it was)
May you see your world in your lifetime
Whisper songs of praise
The Ancient of Days, a name for God (from דניאל ז׳)

steps.confusionAlert: "May you see your world in your lifetime" is not a wish to receive your reward in this world instead of in עולם הבא. The very next line also blesses the learner with עולם הבא. It means you should enjoy good in this world as well.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ מִפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַבִּי אַמֵּי,
phrases.english: When the Sages would take leave of the study hall of Rabbi Ami,
and some say from the study hall of Rabbi Chanina,
they would say to him like this:
"May you see your world in your lifetime,
and may your end be to the life of the World-to-Come,
and may your hope last for many generations.
May your heart think understanding,
your mouth speak wisdom,
and your tongue whisper praises.
May your eyelids look straight ahead of you,
your eyes shine with the light of Torah,
and your face glow like the brightness of the sky.
May your lips pour out knowledge,
your kidneys rejoice in what is upright,
and your feet run to hear
the words of the Ancient of Days."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ מִפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new report, unconnected to the women's promise, describing the Sages' farewell custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן leaving רבי אמי's study hall blessed each other with good in this world, life in עולם הבא, and a body fully devoted to Torah.

steps.title: The farewell blessing at the study hall of רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: When the רבנן left the study hall of רב חסדא (or רבי שמואל בר נחמני), they blessed each other with the פסוק "Our leaders are laden."
steps.simpleTranslation: When the רבנן took leave of the study hall of רב חסדא (some say רבי שמואל בר נחמני), they would say to him: "Our leaders are laden, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second farewell blessing from a different study hall. This one is a short פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing quotes "Our leaders are laden" (תהלים קמ״ד:יד), and the "וגו׳" shows that the rest of the פסוק is included too. What exactly the leaders are "laden" with is disputed. The next two steps give the two explanations: loaded with מצוות, or loaded with יסורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Our leaders, our great ones
Laden, carrying a heavy load
Etc. (the rest of the פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲווֹ מִפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַב חִסְדָּא,
phrases.english: When the Sages would take leave of the study hall of Rav Chisda,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מִבֵּי רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי,
phrases.english: and some say from the study hall of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani,
they would say to him like this:
"Our leaders are laden, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הֲווֹ מִפַּטְרִי רַבָּנַן מִבֵּי רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 19: another study hall's farewell blessing, this time built on a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רבנן leaving רב חסדא's study hall blessed each other with the פסוק "Our leaders are laden" (תהלים קמ״ד:יד).

steps.title: First explanation: leaders in Torah, loaded with מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק "אלופינו מסבלים" and gives the first opinion. "Our leaders" means great in Torah, and "laden" means loaded with מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Our leaders are laden." רב and שמואל argue about this, and some say it was רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר. One said: "Our leaders" means leaders in Torah, and "laden" means loaded with מצוות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the פסוק from the blessing in the last step and starts explaining what it means. It names the two people who argue and gives the first opinion. The second opinion comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has two key words: "אלופינו" (our leaders) and "מסבלים" (laden, carrying a heavy load). In this first view, a person is a "leader" because of his Torah learning, and the "load" he carries is a good one: many מצוות. So the blessing means "may our Torah scholars also be full of מצוות."

keyTerms.meaning: Our leaders or chiefs; here, people who are great in Torah
Laden, carrying a heavy load (from סֵבֶל, a burden)
And some say. Introduces a second version of who said something
One said. Starts the first side of an argument without saying which person holds it

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us which person said which opinion. "חד אמר... וחד אמר" only means "one said... and the other said." Do not try to match the first opinion to רב or the second to שמואל.

phrases.english: "Our leaders are laden":
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק (תהלים קמד:יד) the רבנן used as a blessing in the last step.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel argue about it,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar.
phrases.notes: This gives a second version of who the two people in the argument were.

phrases.english: One said: "Our leaders" means leaders in Torah,
and "laden" means loaded with מצוות.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, חַד אָמַר

steps.title: Second explanation: leaders in Torah and מצוות, loaded with יסורים
steps.stepSummary: The second opinion says "Our leaders" means great in both Torah and מצוות, and "laden" means loaded with יסורים (suffering).
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: "Our leaders" means leaders in Torah and in מצוות, and "laden" means loaded with suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second opinion about the same פסוק. This finishes the argument from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view puts both Torah and מצוות into the word "אלופינו." That leaves "מסבלים" free to mean a new kind of load: יסורים, suffering. Righteous people often carry suffering, so the blessing means "may our great people be able to bear their suffering."

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of "אלופינו מסבלים." (1) Great in Torah, loaded with מצוות. (2) Great in Torah and מצוות, loaded with suffering. The argument is about what the "load" is.
